title: Building a crochet swatch library
subtitle: How to store and label swatches so they become a useful reference rather than discarded scraps
excerpt: A swatch library is a collection of labelled gauge swatches organised by yarn so that the information gathered from each swatch is permanently accessible. Without a library, the gauge work done for one project is lost when the project is finished. A simple labelling system turns discarded swatches into a reference that saves time on every future project that uses the same yarn.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book (Storey Publishing). Pauline Turner, How to Crochet (HarperCollins).

glossaryTerms.definition: A tag attached to a gauge swatch recording the yarn name, weight category, dye lot, hook size used, stitch pattern, pre-block and post-block gauge measurements, and the date. A labelled swatch is useful indefinitely; an unlabelled swatch is useful only while the project is in progress.
The measurement of stitches and rows per 10 cm for a specific yarn-hook-stitch combination after blocking. The core piece of information in a swatch library entry.

content.text: Swatch labels
convert gauge swatches from single-use scraps into a permanent reference. Each swatch records the yarn, hook, stitch, and
gauge record

in a format that is retrievable months later. The benefit is cumulative: after a year of active crocheting, a swatch library means you already know the DK gauge of your favourite yarn in double crochet, treble, and shell stitch before a new project starts.
What to record on each swatch label
Yarn name and brand
Colour name and dye lot number
Hook size in millimetres
Stitch pattern used (double crochet, treble, shell, etc.)
Pre-block gauge: stitches per 10 cm, rows per 10 cm
Post-block gauge: same measurements after blocking
Blocking method used (wet, steam, no-block)
Date the swatch was made
How to make and label the swatches
Work each swatch at least 15 by 15 cm. Smaller swatches give less reliable measurements because the edges affect the reading.
Leave a long tail at the start of the swatch (at least 30 cm). Use this tail to attach the label: write on a card luggage label, punch a hole in it, and tie it to the swatch tail.
Block the swatch the same way you plan to block the finished project.
Measure gauge after blocking and write both pre- and post-block numbers on the label.
Store swatches in a box, binder with plastic pockets, or zip bags organised by yarn brand or weight category.
Common problems

items.symptom: The swatch label information does not match what you remember making
items.cause: The label was written before the swatch was measured and blocked, and the measurements recorded were estimates.
items.fix: Always measure and label after blocking, not before. The post-block gauge is the number the pattern assumes; the pre-block gauge is secondary.

items.symptom: The swatches are disorganised and hard to find
items.fix: Organise by yarn weight category first (lace, DK, aran, chunky), then by yarn brand or name. A labelled box or binder divider per weight category is sufficient.

content.text: What to try next

Go back and label any existing swatches from past projects, even if only with what you can reconstruct from memory. An imperfect label is more useful than no label. From the next new yarn, use the full recording system from the start.
